com.dravensoft.arena.job: read: documentation, reports, changelogs, release notes, any screen somebody reads top to bottom

bw-surface.$description:
The line goes, and unlike the figure/ground voice nothing arrives to replace it.
That is the whole claim: what belongs together is near, what does not is far, and the reader is
trusted to see distance without being shown an edge.

This alone is not proximity, which is why the gate asks for the other two as well. A voice that
removed the line and kept a fill, or kept a depth, would be grouping by region or by figure and
ground with the hairline turned off.

fill-surface.$description:
The card takes the page's own fill, so it stops being a card. A fill is a region
drawn however faint it is: base-200 against base-100 measures 1.07:1 in dark and 1.10:1 in light,
which is nearly invisible and still reads as a container once it has a corner and padding around
it. Nearly invisible is the wrong target here. The target is absent.

fill-surface-floating is deliberately untouched. A menu, a dialog and a toast are separated from
what they cover rather than grouped against it, so they keep a fill of their own; a voice that
flattened them too would have made every overlay unreadable to win an argument about cards. That
split is the reason the two fill roles exist.

pad-surface.$description:
A surface with no line, no depth and no fill has no inside, so it has no room to
give: its content sits on the page directly and lines up with everything else that does. Padding
here would be an indent nobody asked for, and an indent is a weak enclosure, which is the thing
this voice spent its other three decisions removing.

The floating tier has no padding role at all, which is what keeps a dialog from collapsing onto
its own edges when this value goes to zero.

fw-heading.$description:
Once the boxes are gone the type IS the hierarchy, so a heading has to be told
from the text under it by weight alone. 800 to 900, which is the last step the display face has
and the one the wordmark already uses, so nothing here is a value Arena did not already carry.

lh-prose.$description:
1.6 to 1.8, which is the other half of the same decision. A voice that grouped by
distance between blocks and then set its paragraphs tight would be arguing with itself: the air
between lines is the same claim as the air between sections, made at the scale of the sentence.

Well above the 1.5 floor WCAG 1.4.8 asks and check:extensions holds. The floor is a minimum, and
this voice is the one with a reason to sit far from it.

measure-prose.$description:
The one thing this voice was missing and could not say. A voice for reading that
sets the leading of a paragraph and not the length of its lines has answered half of legibility:
a line long enough to lose the return sweep is unreadable at any leading, and documentation runs
to the full width of whatever contains it until something stops it.

68 rather than the 72 the role is born at, because this voice also opens the leading to 1.8. A
looser line wants a shorter measure, since the eye travels further down between one line and the
next and needs less to travel across.

It reaches a page through .arena-prose in css/prose.css, which a consumer puts on the article
they wrote. Arena ships no prose component, and this is the one voice whose whole job is markup
Arena does not own.

lh-heading.$description:
Titles packed against paragraphs opened up, which is the contrast this voice
carries its hierarchy in once it has no lines to draw one with. 1.15 against 1.8 is a difference
a reader sees without being able to name.

Not lh.tight, which is 0.98 and would put a two-line title's own lines through each other. The
floor check:extensions holds at 1 is what caught that, and it is worth recording that the first
draft of this voice reached for tight before the gate existed.

ff-eyebrow.$description:
In a document an eyebrow is an antetitle, the line that says which chapter this
is. It is prose about prose. The mono face reads as a system tag, which is the register of a
console rather than of a page somebody sits down with, so this voice takes it into the body face
with everything else it expects to be read.

tt-eyebrow.$description:
Capitals are the other half of that register, and they cost reading speed: a word
in capitals loses the ascender and descender pattern a reader recognises it by. A voice for
reading has the least reason of any to spend that.

track-eyebrow.$description:
The open tracking exists to make capitals legible, and this voice just dropped
the capitals. Left where it was it would read as a line somebody spaced out on purpose, which is
the look of a caption in a fashion magazine and not of a heading in a changelog. The three move
together or none of them should.

ink-muted.$description:
A colour that is genuinely held back, rather than the page's own ink at a
percentage. The difference matters most in this voice: with no card behind it, muted text sits
directly on the page, and base-content at 62 percent over base-100 is the same hue thinned rather
than a second voice speaking quietly.

It is an assignment, like every colour role: the value is the consumer's neutral-content, and
check:text-contrast measures the level it lands at once per theme.

rhythm-group.$description:
Tighter than the default, and that is half of the mechanism. Proximity says two
things are one by putting them near each other, so near has to be nearer than it needs to be when
a box is doing the work as well.

rhythm-component.$description:
Two peer components separated by twice the air inside one of them is not a step a
reader sees, and this voice has no line to fall back on when the distance fails. Widened until
the ladder reads: 8px inside a group, 24px between peers, 64px between sections, which is 1 to 3
to 8. The default ladder can afford to be gentler because a hairline is carrying the grouping
beside it.

rhythm-section.$description:
The far end of the ladder. 8px inside a group against 64px between sections is a ratio of
eight, where the default is two and the figure/ground voice is a little over three. Distance is
the ONLY signal this voice has left, so it has to carry a hierarchy that the other two spend
lines, fills and shadows on, and a ratio that reads as a hierarchy is what pays for the edge that
is no longer drawn. check:extensions holds it above four for exactly that reason.

step-title-page.$description:
A document's own title, set as one. With no lines and no fills the ladder IS the
hierarchy, so the rung a page opens on has to be further from the section under it than a voice
with boxes needs it to be: 64 over 24 is the same argument the rhythm ladder makes at 8 to 64.

It moves alone. The section and the surface rungs stay where they are, because widening the gap
at the top is what says a page has a title, and widening every gap would just enlarge the page.

r-media.$description:
A figure in a document is not enclosed either. This voice spent bw-surface,
fill-surface and pad-surface removing the box from around a card, and a rounded corner on a
screenshot is the same box drawn one more time. Square, so a diagram sits on the page the way a
paragraph does.

Authored outright rather than aliased, because the radius scale starts at 4 and the claim here is
not a smaller corner but no corner.

fit-media.$description:
A figure in a document is a diagram, a screenshot or a chart, and the whole of it
is the point. Cropping the edges off a screenshot to fill a frame loses the part that was being
pointed at, which is a different failure from a product photograph losing its background.

It pairs with the ratio below: a contained image inside a frame that is not its shape letterboxes
rather than crops, and a document would rather show the whole thing than the right rectangle.

aspect-media.$description:
Sixteen by ten, which is the shape of the thing a document usually shows: a
window, a screen, a chart wider than it is tall. The square this is born at is the shape of a
product in a grid, and a screenshot cropped to one is a screenshot with its sides cut off.
